resident.scope:
Paired, bounded native collection acceptance across three public call paths.

This measures a deterministic 32-row held-out fixture, not ClickBench, broad SQL,
native Python bindings, process-wide memory enforcement, or a production workload.

surfaces.fresh_cli_process: native process creation through complete stdout and process exit
surfaces.persistent_worker: request JSON encoding/write through complete response line; worker startup separate
surfaces.python_client: public_workflow_run argument construction, worker roundtrip and typed envelope parsing; import excluded

resident.cache_policy: OS page cache uncontrolled; one source artifact; no query-answer reuse

native_resident.cache_policy: provider reader/layout metadata reused; OS cache uncontrolled; no result cache

native_count_report.timing_boundary: prepared full predicate scan or metadata pruning through complete scalar/report/native certificate return; verification and returned report drop excluded

filtered_count.transport_comparison: requires identical fixture and predicate; do not subtract unlike workload timing surfaces

metadata_count.timing_boundary: prepared native footer count including admission and source generation validation

native_resident.scope: prepared Rust metadata/optional full filtered count/bounded array and JSON calls; not Python, fresh-process, mixed-load or durable ingest latency

release_experiments.process_scope: RSS and user/system CPU belong to each complete multi-variant test process; never assign these peaks to individual variants.

numeric.correctness_proof: Successful frozen test asserts full COUNT/MIN/MAX/SUM state equality after each pair, total canonical/selected rows, and the maximum canonical block size; JSON has no separate value-verification flag.
numeric.limitations: One BitPacked fixture and one additive measure; state consumers are existing typed loops. Bounded arm includes its block/row assertions inside the clock. Whole-array and bounded temporary-owner lifetimes differ inside their respective native calls. No per-variant RSS, file query, independent CPU-time, or universal throughput claim.

compact.timer_scope: retained actual reducer lifecycle including routing/locks/credit publication and consumed native partial disposal; candidate test adapter updates plus separately reported routing; native fixture/hash/oracle/export construction excluded; not isolated table-kernel or public query latency
compact.input_disposal_scope: retained reduce consumes/disposes native value/count partial inside reduce clock; candidate borrowed routing vectors dispose outside update clock; no direct table-speed attribution
compact.memory_scope: explicit state table/arena and partition metadata capacities; source/partial/input routing/oracle/output/provider/allocator overhead and RSS excluded
compact.counter_scope: retained copy sites are cfg(test) instrumented; retained probes unavailable; full-hash equality is not total probes; candidate lookup excludes rehash probes
compact.lifecycle_sum_scope: Arithmetic sum of named construction, arrange+reduce/update, and state drop clocks; not continuous wall time. Candidate source/routing disposal is outside its update clock, unlike retained native-partial disposal inside reduce.

owner.scope: actual retained partition reducer, identical prepared native ranges; source construction/hash/arrange and full oracle/export excluded; prior full output retained symmetrically; no compact-state or public-query claim
owner.timing_scope: wall clocks; dequeue includes idle waits and lock acquisition includes uncontended acquisition; no CPU-time or cache-cold claim
owner.memory_scope: actual table/arena credits plus reserved range queue/control envelopes; fixture provider buffers, OS thread stacks, ComputePool internal bookkeeping and output oracle maps excluded
owner.limitations: Reducer work/lock/queue counter clocks can overlap across workers; sums are not exclusive CPU time. Existing partition locks remain in both variants. Preparation, complete-value export and oracle are excluded. No claim about public scan scheduling or whole-query latency.
